label: late input positions (t>=6) and the <DEL> step, boosted by y/3/e/u/2/t/g/j
explanation: Absolute-position unit. It is silent at t<=4 and almost silent in the copy phase (0.6% of mass, mostly recall_idx 1). It fires on late original-phase inputs (orig_idx 5-8, rate rising from 2% to 53%) and on the <DEL> step (30% rate, 45% of mass). So it is mostly a longer-sequence feature: L=9 carries 56% of mass and L<=5 carries none. Within this window, the input token sets how likely it is to fire. y, 3, e, u, 2, t, g and j have the highest rates and the same tokens in prev_tok/prev2_tok also raise it, so the gate seems to build up over a run of these tokens. The strongest examples are <DEL> or late inputs following several of them. In-window steps where in_tok is the first occurrence of that token make up 87% of mass. The position window by itself has recall 0.96 but precision 0.37, and adding the token set gives dev F1 0.63. The token dependence is graded and was only partly captured, so precision stays near 0.5.
